story.title: Lionel Messi Retires from International Football After 21 Years
story.summary: Lionel Messi has announced his retirement from international football at the age of 39, concluding a remarkable 21-year career with Argentina. He leaves as the nation's record appearance holder and top scorer, having recently led the team to the 2026 World Cup final. Messi expressed that the decision was difficult but felt it was the right time to step away from the national team.

event_overview.title: About International Soccer
event_overview.subject: International Soccer
event_overview.summary: This event concerns Lionel Messi’s reported decision to end his international career with Argentina’s senior men’s national team, following a tenure that began with his debut in August 2005. It marks a national-team career rather than a retirement from all professional club football, and follows a period in which Messi was central to Argentina’s major tournament successes.

facts.label: International-career dates
facts.value: Messi made his senior Argentina debut against Hungary in Budapest on 17 August 2005; the selected timeline places the reported end of that international career on 31 August 2026.

facts.label: National-team context
facts.value: Argentina’s national side is administered by the Argentine Football Association (AFA), one of FIFA’s member associations; FIFA’s member associations organize and govern football within their territories.

facts.label: Major senior honours
facts.value: During Messi’s Argentina career, the team won the 2021 Copa América in Brazil and the 2022 FIFA World Cup in Qatar; FIFA describes him as Argentina’s captain during this successful period.

facts.label: International-football governance
facts.value: FIFA is the global governing body whose statutes and regulations govern international association football, while national associations participate through six continental confederations, including South America’s CONMEBOL.

event_overview.scope_note: The selected Muninn timeline covers the reported retirement announcement and immediate related developments, not Messi’s full club career, every Argentina match, or the broader history of international football.

explore_lenses.label: What is Messi’s next competitive step?
explore_lenses.title: Club football continues with Inter Miami
explore_lenses.summary: Messi’s announcement ends his Argentina career, not his playing career. His immediate competitive focus remains Inter Miami’s 2026 MLS campaign, where he had just produced a four-goal, one-assist performance.

claims.text: Major League Soccer named Messi its Player of the Matchday after he scored four goals and made one assist in Inter Miami’s 7-1 win over CF Montréal on August 29, 2026.
The supplied Africanews report says Messi remains an Inter Miami player and that his international retirement does not end his club career.

explore_lenses.label: How did Argentina reach this farewell?
explore_lenses.title: From 2016 setback to a trophy-laden exit
explore_lenses.summary: The retirement follows a career that moved from an earlier international exit after the 2016 Copa América final to a run of major titles and a sixth World Cup appearance. The 2026 final was Messi’s last Argentina match, rather than a title-winning farewell.

claims.text: Messi’s final international match was Argentina’s 1-0 extra-time loss to Spain in the FIFA World Cup final on July 19, 2026; Ferran Torres scored in the 106th minute.

Africanews reports that Messi briefly retired after Argentina lost the 2016 Copa América final to Chile, then returned and helped Argentina win the 2021 Copa América, the 2022 World Cup and the 2024 Copa América.
Messi said the decision still hurt but that he felt the time had come, adding that he had always given everything for Argentina’s shirt.
He leaves as Argentina’s record appearance-maker and scorer, with 207 caps and 125 goals, according to Reuters reporting carried by Investing.com.

explore_lenses.label: Who could fill Messi’s attacking role?
explore_lenses.title: Argentina has options, but no named successor
explore_lenses.summary: Argentina’s World Cup squad included several established forwards and younger attacking players, giving coach Lionel Scaloni personnel options. That does not amount to an announced one-for-one replacement for Messi’s captaincy, creativity or status.

claims.text: FIFA’s pre-tournament Argentina squad overview identified Julián Álvarez, Lautaro Martínez, Thiago Almada, Nico Paz and José Manuel López among the attacking options selected by Scaloni for the 2026 World Cup.

FIFA reported that Argentina used every outfield player in its 2026 World Cup group stage, with Messi still involved, indicating that Scaloni had already given minutes to a broader group during the tournament.

Rodrigo De Paul, Leandro Paredes and Cristian Romero praised or thanked Messi after the announcement, while the Argentine Football Association paid tribute to his representation of the country, according to Africanews.

story_report.summary: Lionel Messi has retired from international football at 39, ending a 21-year Argentina career in which he became the country’s record appearance-maker and leading scorer. His departure follows Argentina’s run to the 2026 World Cup final and closes a national-team career that included major tournament victories after an earlier, brief retirement in 2016. The decision removes Messi from Argentina selection, but it does not end his club career with Inter Miami.

sections.heading: Messi’s Return Brought Major Titles
sections.body: Messi briefly stepped away from Argentina duty after the 2016 Copa América final loss to Chile before returning to the national side. He subsequently helped Argentina win the 2021 Copa América, the 2022 World Cup and the 2024 Copa América. In explaining his latest decision, Messi said it still hurt but that the time had come, adding that he had always given everything for Argentina’s shirt.

sections.heading: Messi’s Final Match Ended in Defeat
sections.body: Messi’s last Argentina appearance was the 2026 World Cup final, where Spain beat Argentina 1-0 after extra time on July 19. Ferran Torres scored the deciding goal in the 106th minute. Messi finishes with 207 caps and 125 goals, according to Reuters reporting carried by Investing.com, while Rodrigo De Paul, Leandro Paredes and Cristian Romero were among those who praised or thanked him after the announcement.

sections.heading: Argentina Retains Several Attacking Options
sections.body: Argentina coach Lionel Scaloni had already used every outfield player during the 2026 World Cup group stage, with Messi still involved. FIFA’s pre-tournament squad overview listed Julián Álvarez, Lautaro Martínez, Thiago Almada, Nico Paz and José Manuel López among the attacking options. At club level, Messi recently scored four goals and supplied an assist in Inter Miami’s 7-1 victory over CF Montréal, earning MLS Player of the Matchday recognition.

The consulted sources do not establish how long Messi plans to continue playing for Inter Miami or whether he will make a future club-retirement announcement.

related_stories.title: Supreme Court Allows Trump to Continue White House Ballroom Construction
related_stories.summary: The US Supreme Court has permitted the continuation of construction on a $400 million ballroom project at the White House, initiated by Trump. However, the court did not make a ruling on the legality of the project. Chief Justice John Roberts expressed dissent, stating that the construction is likely unlawful.
